quarterly_data.signal: CEO view on hybrid-bonding adoption: hybrid bonding has become a critical enabler of next-generation chip architectures (density, performance, thermal management). AMD started shipping hybrid-bonded logic devices in 2022; Apple, Intel and Broadcom all have products ramping into production using hybrid bonding. He believes hybrid bonding will be a requirement in HBM with 20 or more layers, if not sooner, and in NAND as layer counts approach 400, with the big three memory players all ramping to get there. Leading foundries, memory companies and OSATs are planning to spend approximately $125 billion in the near term on advanced packaging including hybrid bonding — 'we know broad adoption of hybrid bonding is coming because the capital equipment required is being ordered.' Hyperscalers 'are semiconductor companies now', differentiating with their own chips, which he expects to create additional opportunity. He puts the semiconductor market at over $1.5 trillion this year.

quarterly_data.signal: THE CAPITAL RAISE IS A SUBSTRATE-AND-FAB SPENDING EVENT: Zinsner explained the August equity raise as 'the capital raise precedes capital investment' - 2026 CapEx has already been upticked 'by a couple of billion dollars from $18 billion to $20 billion', next year's will be significantly higher, and 'substrates are really constrained and we're going to need to make investments associated with substrates as well next year, given the significant demand.' Committing to 14A high-volume manufacturing in 2028 means placing long-lead supplier orders now, which was one of the biggest drivers of the raise. On footprint: Ireland's shell is being equipped now; Fab 52 in Arizona is running Intel 18A and Fab 62 is almost ready, with next year's investment accelerating its equipping; Oregon stays the pilot line but will also run volume Intel 14A as 18A is pushed into Arizona; Ohio shells are in progress with the ability to have 'eight mods, or there is two mods per fab, so four fabs in Ohio', mod one being built as fast as possible. Zinsner said 2027 CapEx is not locked - the businesses gave him a number and 'I've told them no', sending them back for more efficiency before he guides.
quarterly_data.figure: from $18 billion to $20 billion; eight mods, or there is two mods per fab, so four fabs in Ohio

quarterly_data.signal: INTEL 14A: 0.9 PDK IN OCTOBER, RISK PRODUCTION 2027, HIGH-VOLUME 2028: Zinsner said Intel is within two months of the 14A 0.9 PDK, so 'you can pretty much now expect us to land in October with that 0.9 PDK', and the remaining step from 0.9 to 1.0 is much smaller than 0.5 to 0.9. Defect density on Intel 14A is tracking better than the target curve and is coming down faster than any previous node - 'we haven't seen this performance since 22 nanometer, which is arguably one of the best nodes Intel's ever put out' - while 18A yields are beating internal milestones. Demand side: internal product teams, 'probably the most cynical bunch out of anybody', are now designing products on Intel 14A, and external foundry engagements have increased enough that Lip-Bu Tan and the team meet customers weekly and the conversation has moved from data to 'how much capacity can I get? What does that supply look like?'. That sequence forces risk production in 2027 ahead of high-volume manufacturing in 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: 0.9 PDK in October; risk production in 2027; high volume production in 2028; 22 nanometer

quarterly_data.signal: EMIB-T ADVANCED PACKAGING SIZED FOR THE FIRST TIME - REVENUE FROM 2H 2027, MULTIPLE BILLIONS PER CUSTOMER: Zinsner said EMIB-T, which removes the interposer from EMIB and can increase reticle size significantly, is a differentiated solution not available elsewhere, and that packaging revenue will 'start to ramp in the back half of 2027', become a run-rate business in 2028 and be 'definitely hitting its stride in 2029'. Scale: 'this business is in the billions... by customer, it will be multiple billion dollars per customer per year of business', at margins of '40% gross, 30% operating margin' with low capital intensity relative to the front end, so 'the ROIC is phenomenal'. He framed advanced packaging as the on-ramp that tests Intel operationally and creates cross-sell into front-end foundry, something Intel has 'already seen that show up even now'. He also pointed to the hire of Seokhee, former CEO of SK hynix, to lead the business as the signal of the opportunity size.
quarterly_data.figure: back half of 2027; multiple billion dollars per customer per year; 40% gross, 30% operating margin

quarterly_data.signal: INTEL 3 OFFERED AS A BASE-DIE PROCESS FOR OTHER COMPANIES: Asked whether the Ireland Intel 3/4 nodes are internal-only, CFO David Zinsner said 'Intel 3 would not be a great logic process for external, but we use it for base die, and it can be used for base die for other companies. And the fact that we have advanced packaging and all these things kind of all under one roof, there could potentially be some opportunities there.'
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: COMPONENT SQUEEZE - DRAM, NAND AND SUBSTRATES: CFO Zinsner said 'over the last several months, industry-wide supply for key components like DRAM, NAND and substrates has come under increasing pressure due to intense demand to support the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure', and rising component pricing, especially relative to the client market, 'could limit our revenue opportunity this year'. CEO Tan called the memory constraint and pricing 'a very big challenge' for the industry: bigger OEM and hyperscale players have more access to memory while smaller ones 'are really challenging to scramble to get the memory', so Intel is allocating CPUs to customers that can complete products ('We don't want to have a CPU, we sent to them, but they are missing the memory'). CFO Zinsner added that for Lunar Lake, Intel was 'relatively aggressive in terms of getting the memory early', though those margins are low because the memory is in package.

Strengths it claims: void-free copper filling of the holes formed in glass, smaller holes relative to substrate thickness (aspect ratio) at higher hole density, and long experience handling thin glass substrates up to three meters square from its color-filter business. The glass-core business is classed as a growth-potential business.

quarterly_data.signal: 1.6T optical-module PCB: current orders are mainly 1.6T high-speed optical-module boards; 2026 optical-module related revenue is guided to double, 1.6T keeps growing sharply in 2027 and becomes the main shipping spec in 2028, and 3.2T boards are already being sampled. Customers are already pre-booking 2027 capacity; target is to become the world's largest high-end optical-module PCB supplier in 2027. 800G-and-above optical-module boards require M7-class ultra-low-loss laminate (1.6T effectively mandates it); management says roughly 20 players claim to be entering optical modules but few master M7 high-layer board production, which is why Zhen Ding's substrate-derived M7 technology gave it the 1.6T breakout. 1.6T optical-module board yield is described as industry-leading at above 90%, including the newly ramped Thailand lines. On a potential US FCC ban on Chinese optical modules: Zhen Ding supplies the PCB inside the module, not the module itself, so sees no direct hit, and can shift production to Thailand where customers require it. On CPO: the company says it will participate in both pluggable and CPO/NPO architectures as they develop; most PCB equipment is transferable between product types so a CPO shift would strand little capacity.

Thailand: PA01 reached breakeven and turned profitable in July 2026 (mass production began Q3 2025); additional Thai buildings and a data/computing center complete around end-2026; Thai plants 1-2 make server and optical-module boards, plant 3 flex, plant 4 high-layer-count server boards. Shenzhen third campus broke ground 07-24-2026 for AI 1.6T optical-module high-layer boards and high-end AI flex; its supplier conference drew 217 supply-chain companies and 410 representatives. Capacity for the next three years is largely bound to customers through LTAs and project-based binding agreements (visibility to 2029); 2027 AI PCB order visibility described as optimistic with capacity still insufficient. By 2030 the target is server + optical-module + IC-substrate at 45% to 50% of group revenue. GPU customer motherboards are produced both in mainland China and Thailand depending on customer requirements. quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 results (company investor deck, June 2026): revenue NT$40,728 million, up 1.6% YoY and a record for the period; gross profit NT$8,812 million (+49.7% YoY), gross margin 21.6% vs 14.7% a year earlier (a record for the period per the company); operating profit NT$2,503 million (+137.1%), operating margin 6.1% (+3.5 ppts); net income to parent NT$1,426 million (+125.4%), EPS NT$1.33 vs NT$0.66. Server/Optical revenue more than doubled YoY and IC Substrate revenue grew over 60% YoY; together they were nearly 20% of Q1 revenue (19.7% on the deck's chart). Q1 2026 revenue by application: Mobile Communication 54.5%, Computers and Consumer Electronics 25.8%, IC Substrate 9.6%, Server/Optical & Others 10.1%. The deck also states 2025 IC substrate revenue grew 31.3% YoY.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 2026 revenue NT$40,728 million (+1.6% YoY); gross margin 21.6%; operating margin 6.1%; EPS NT$1.33; Server/Optical + IC Substrate 19.7% of revenue

quarterly_data.signal: Company outlook (June 2026 investor deck): from Q2, customers' next-generation AI platforms gradually enter mass production, driving significant quarter-by-quarter growth in the Server/Optical business, with full-year 2026 Server/Optical revenue expected to more than double. Full-year 2026 IC Substrate revenue is targeted to grow 80%+, with revenue expected to increase sequentially through the year as demand and order visibility improve (the company says it has deep collaborations with multiple customers on high-end AI-related products). Citing clear long-term cooperation visibility with several key customers on mid- to long-term AI demand, Zhen Ding raised its 2026 capital expenditure plan from NT$50 billion+ to NT$80 billion+, focused on AI servers, optical communications, IC substrates and Edge AI; its stated goal is to make Huai'an Tech City the world's largest and most technologically advanced single-site PCB manufacturing base.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 Server/Optical revenue expected to more than double; 2026 IC Substrate revenue target +80%+; 2026 capex plan raised from NT$50 billion+ to NT$80 billion+

quarterly_data.signal: Products and capacity (June 2026 investor deck): iHDI and HLC products for GPU and ASIC AI-server customers are gradually entering mass production, with development continuing for the next two to three platform generations; optical-communication orders are driven primarily by 1.6T high-speed boards, revenue is expected to grow multiple-fold YoY in 2026 and customers have begun reserving 2027 capacity. ABF substrates currently achieve a maximum body size of 158 x 158 mm and up to 28 layers (company: cutting-edge industry capability); new ABF capacity is to support penetration into major international customers. Shenzhen ABF Fab 1 turned profitable in 1Q26, and based on clear customer demand the company has initiated installation of Shenzhen ABF Fab 2. BT substrate utilization remains high, with debottlenecking capacity expansion planned at the Qinhuangdao facility in 1H26. Huai'an: RMB 19 billion planned from 2H25 to 2029 to expand high-end PCB capacity, with six new iHDI and HLC facilities planned for completion by end-2026. Thailand fab 1 focuses on high-end iHDI, HLC and optical-module products; the company has passed qualification and entered mass production with multiple customers, and several leading global server and optical customers are in active qualification.
quarterly_data.figure: ABF substrate up to 158 x 158 mm and 28 layers; Huai'an RMB 19 billion (2H25-2029); six new iHDI/HLC facilities by end-2026; Shenzhen ABF Fab 1 profitable in 1Q26

quarterly_data.signal: Global capacity roadmap (September 2026 investor deck): Zhen Ding shows 28 plants in 2026 growing to 57 plants by 2030 (13 new plants under construction and another 16 plants in the planning stage).
quarterly_data.figure: 28 plants (2026) to 57 plants (2030)

quarterly_data.figure: Q2 capex NT$17,009 million (+94.4% YoY); H1 capex NT$29,688 million (+106.3%); Q2 operating margin 7.8%; Q2 EPS NT$2.19

quarterly_data.signal: Optical boards and capacity (results deck): for optical modules, 1.6T and subsequent generations require mSAP technology; the company says demand for high-end optical-module PCBs continues to outstrip supply globally and it is expanding related capacity. Thailand: Fab 1 (high-end HDI, HLC and optical-module products, mass production since 3Q25); three additional fabs and one mechanical drilling center are under construction, with trial production expected to start progressively from 4Q26. Shenzhen Campus III smart manufacturing base (broke ground July 2026) will comprise three plants focused on high-end substrate-like PCBs for AI servers and optical modules, plus advanced FPCs for AI devices. New capacity comes online in phases from 2026 to 2030 in line with customer qualification and mass-production schedules.

players.product: High-complexity multilayer PCBs, substrates and advanced packaging for AI data-center/networking systems

quarterly_data.signal: All-time record quarter: sales $846M (+30% YoY), non-GAAP EPS $0.75 (+50%). DATA CENTER & NETWORKING grew 61% YoY (36% of sales, expected to reach 42% in Q2) on AI buildouts — the US PCB/substrate pure-play angle. Commercial book-to-bill 1.65 (overall 1.41); 90-day backlog $787M vs $517M a year ago. ~80% of net sales tied to the AI + defense megatrends; multi-year plan reiterated: revenue +15-20%/yr for 3 years and DOUBLE earnings from 2025 to 2027 — 'tracking well ahead'.
quarterly_data.figure: DC/networking +61% YoY (42% of Q2 sales); commercial B2B 1.65; backlog $787M

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity racing demand: FY2026 capex plan raised from ~$250M midpoint to ~$310M to secure equipment and accelerate revenue; Penang (Malaysia) ramping with 'one of the data-center networking players' as anchor customer + new R&D center; 24 manufacturing sites across China/Malaysia/Canada/US gives customers geographic supply options. Strategy moving up-stack from advanced interconnect (complex PCBs, substrates, advanced packaging) into modules/subsystems combining sensors, RF and PHOTONICS.
quarterly_data.figure: Capex raised to ~$310M; Penang ramp w/ DC-networking anchor customer

quarterly_data.signal: First-ever $1 billion quarter: Q2 net sales of $1.0 billion, up 37% year over year from $731 million, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.99 per diluted share, up 71% - both all-time highs and both above guidance. Adjusted EBITDA was $166.8 million or 16.6% of sales, up 160 basis points year over year and 90 basis points sequentially on favourable mix. Non-GAAP gross margin was 21.9% (+100bps) and operating margin 13.8% (+270bps) on volume, mix and SG&A discipline. GAAP operating income was $109.1 million and GAAP EPS $0.77. Management reiterated that roughly 80% of net sales are tied to the AI and defense megatrends.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 sales $1.0B (+37% YoY); non-GAAP EPS $0.99 (+71%); adjusted EBITDA $166.8M (16.6%, +160bps YoY)

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 guidance: net sales of $1.10-1.14 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $1.21-1.27, with a further sequential uptick expected in Q4. Full-year 2026 is now guided to approximately $4.4 billion of sales with non-GAAP EPS approaching $5 - both excluding any contribution from the pending European acquisitions - versus the previously communicated plan of at least $4 billion. Management reaffirmed confidence in 15% to 20% ORGANIC revenue growth for both 2027 and 2028, with further clarity promised next quarter alongside an updated long-term plan. Q3 assumes ~107.7 million diluted shares, SG&A ~7% of sales, R&D ~1%, and a 13-17% tax rate.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 guide $1.10B-$1.14B, EPS $1.21-$1.27; FY2026 ~$4.4B sales, EPS approaching $5; 15-20% organic growth reaffirmed for 2027-2028

quarterly_data.signal: Data center and networking was 40% of Q2 sales and grew 91% year over year, above expectations, on AI data-center build-out demand. It is guided to 49% of net sales in Q3 as the N+M ramp begins, and full-year 2026 sales in the end market are now expected to MORE THAN DOUBLE year over year. On customer concentration, TTM has one 10% customer in commercial and one in aerospace and defense, with another commercial customer approaching 10%; management described the commercial roster as 'getting a bit crowded,' with 10-plus large hyperscaler and networking companies in the field.
quarterly_data.figure: Data center & networking 40% of Q2 sales, +91% YoY; guided to 49% of Q3 sales; FY2026 to more than double

quarterly_data.signal: N+M asymmetrical interconnect printed circuit boards entered the early stage of full production launch. TTM has already delivered 'tens of millions' with yields running better than planned, and about $600 MILLION of N+M is scheduled for the second half of 2026 - roughly one third in Q3 and two thirds in Q4 - with adjusted EBITDA margins improving as the yield curve improves. CEO Edwin Roks stressed N+M is 'not just one process, it's a family of different options' and only the first step, supporting multiple customers beyond data center and networking. Asked whether an incremental $1 billion of N+M revenue in 2027 was the right figure, Roks said it 'could be in the ballpark,' with the precise number pending the bottom-up annual plan.
quarterly_data.figure: ~$600M of N+M in H2 2026 (1/3 Q3, 2/3 Q4); 2027 incremental N+M 'could be in the ballpark' of $1B

quarterly_data.signal: Order book at record levels: overall book-to-bill was 1.49 in Q2 (commercial segment 1.63, aerospace and defense 1.3). The 90-day backlog, which is subject to cancellation, was $901 million versus $497 million a year ago - an 81% increase. The aerospace and defense total program backlog rose to $1.7 billion from $1.5 billion a year ago, and qualified business proposals in the A&D strategic pipeline are at an all-time high of over $7 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: Book-to-bill 1.49 (commercial 1.63, A&D 1.3); 90-day backlog $901M (+81% YoY); A&D program backlog $1.7B; >$7B qualified A&D pipeline

quarterly_data.signal: Laminate material supply is tightening at the low end, not the high end. CCL (copper-clad laminate) producers are shifting away from lower-complexity materials toward higher-complexity products, which puts slight pressure on material availability - felt in automotive and other lower-end parts of the portfolio rather than in the high-end data center materials such as T-glass. Management said lead times remain decent, high-end materials are available, customers are not suffering, and TTM is actively working with supply chain partners to secure supply in line with customer demand. Automotive is guided to about 6% of Q3 sales partly because of this dynamic.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity build-out: the new Syracuse facility begins initial volume ramp of Ultra-HDI products in Q3, continuing through Q4 and 2027 to reach full capacity run rate in 2028. Penang is at 'very decent revenue levels' and close to breakeven, expected late Q3 or Q4; it now runs N+M - one of the most difficult technologies in the company - and supports some data center and networking customers alongside its core medical/instrumentation/industrial base. The Wisconsin (Eau Claire) site, bought for less than $20 million, will host some production plus an innovation center near Chippewa Falls, deliberately unrushed. Growth capacity is coming mainly from brownfield expansion of existing sites, particularly in China, and the board approved accelerated capital expenditure that raises the full-year 2026 capex range by around $45 million at both ends.
quarterly_data.figure: Syracuse Ultra-HDI full run rate 2028; Penang breakeven late Q3/Q4; FY2026 capex range raised ~$45M

quarterly_data.signal: Aerospace and defense was 37% of Q2 sales and grew 14% year over year on defense budget tailwinds and program alignment. Q2 bookings included the APS-153 multi-mode maritime surveillance radar, the ATP Sensor System for targeting and surveillance, Golden Dome and a number of restricted priority programs. The segment is guided to about 32% of Q3 sales with continued year-on-year and sequential growth, and full-year 2026 growth in the low to mid teens. The business splits between Ultra-HDI PCBs and 'up-the-chain' RF modules, subsystems and complete radar systems, both performing well.
quarterly_data.figure: A&D 37% of Q2 sales, +14% YoY; guided ~32% of Q3 sales; FY2026 growth low-to-mid teens

quarterly_data.signal: TTM announced its intention to acquire two privately held European companies - Swiss Technology Group AG (STG) in Switzerland and ILFA GmbH in Germany - with the transaction expected to close in Q3 2026 pending regulatory clearance. Together they represent less than 5% of incremental sales and are expected to be moderately accretive on an adjusted EBITDA basis, establishing TTM's first European footprint in long-cycle medical and A&D businesses. Q2 GAAP results included a $14 million non-cash pretax unrealized loss from a deal-contingent cross-currency swap hedging the Swiss-franc purchase price, which could not receive hedge accounting because the deal had not closed.
quarterly_data.figure: STG + ILFA: <5% incremental sales, closing Q3 2026; $14M non-cash swap loss in Q2 GAAP results

quarterly_data.signal: Medical, industrial and instrumentation grew 33% year over year, helped by healthy medical demand including major continuous glucose monitoring products and by instrumentation for AUTOMATED TEST EQUIPMENT SUPPORTING AI SOLUTIONS. Year to date the top five medical customers have more than doubled internal expectations, with further growth expected from surgical robots, electrophysiology and continuous glucose measurement. The end market is guided to 13% of Q3 sales and full-year 2026 growth of 35% to 40%. Automotive was 8% of Q2 sales and marginally down year over year, with full-year sales still expected to decline mid single digits as TTM stays selective on higher-value work.
quarterly_data.figure: MI&I +33% YoY, FY2026 growth 35-40%, guided to 13% of Q3 sales; automotive 8% of Q2 sales, FY2026 down mid-single digits

quarterly_data.signal: THE SHAPE OF THE DATA-CENTER CUSTOMER BASE (CEO Edwin Roks): TTM will not name customers - 'we cannot disclose our customers. We have very strict NDAs with them. But these are the big guys. These are the big guys you read in the newspaper every day, correct? 10, 15 of these big customers, and then a tail of another 50. Which is helping us to understand the landscape, to understand what are the trends.' On hyperscaler roadmap alignment: 'the first thing what we do is align with our customers, and these are the multiple hyperscalers. We also like to show, let's say, demonstrators. I hate to go with only PowerPoints to our customers... So alignment with these hyperscalers, by the way, with all our customers, is going very well.' Management also framed N+M as the start of a technology curve rather than a one-off: 'where you do N+M, which is a new technology, only the first generation of that new technology trend, is working out very well. We're ramping up.'
quarterly_data.figure: 10, 15 of these big customers, and then a tail of another 50

quarterly_data.quarter: TTM Technologies Jefferies Global Industrials Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: DATA CENTER AND NETWORKING IS SET TO OUTGROW DEFENSE INTO THE MIX (CEO): asked about the long-term split of the ~80% of the business tied to AI and aerospace/defense, which is roughly even today, 'If you look at how fast data centers and networking is growing right now, it will likely get aerospace and defense to a 30% portion. Now it's 40%. But who cares, because the business is growing nicely in double digits, and it is very sustainable.' The strategic direction is away from a pure PCB identity: 'we are indeed coming from a traditional PCB company, but we have to find another word for PCB... We're moving into, let's say, a more, I would say, communication and sensing company' - built on heterogeneous, very compact packaging and then modules, subsystems and systems, plus geographic expansion into Europe where management expects to do more acquisitions. The CEO's framing of the AI role: with Moore's law slowing, 'What we provide is, let's say, combining these chips. That's why we like to call ourselves the nervous system... combining these chips in a very efficient way with low latency and high bandwidth.'

contracts.signal: 20-F: since 1997 ASE has maintained a strategic alliance with TSMC, which designates ASE as its non-exclusive preferred provider of packaging and testing services for semiconductors manufactured by TSMC; ASE receives wafers from customers or foundries on a consignment basis.

quarterly_data.signal: Advanced packaging capacity is 'VERY TIGHT also' — TSMC is working with OSAT partners to increase capacity on top of its own expansion. Supplies the LARGEST reticle-size packaging today (large CoWoS); CoPoS pilot line is built NOW with production expected 'a couple of years later'; SoIC and system-on-wafer also in the toolkit. Key engineering challenges at giant die sizes: mechanical stress, warpage and thermal limitation — 'the harder the better'. Note: customers exploring competitor EMIB for larger reticle sizes; TSMC says it leaves no business on the table.
quarterly_data.figure: Adv packaging very tight; CoPoS pilot now -> production ~2028

quarterly_data.signal: PACKAGING IS NOW THE BINDING CONSTRAINT — CEO C.C. Wei, asked about competitors' EMIB-T gaining traction: 'our PACKAGING CAPACITY IS SO TIGHT that now it's LIMITING MY CUSTOMERS' GROWTH. We welcome that additional flexibility in the market. That will help TSMC's front-end wafer business growth, which is a majority part of TSMC's business... We hope they will be successful, that share some of the loading from TSMC. Today, we're working very hard to shorten the gap between the demand and the capacity.' TSMC is explicitly willing to let a rival packaging technology absorb overflow because front-end wafer is the larger profit pool. Capacity response: the newly announced ADDITIONAL $100 BILLION ARIZONA INVESTMENT includes ADVANCED PACKAGING FABS alongside 2nm-and-below logic fabs, and 13 leading-edge and advanced-packaging fabs are being built in Taiwan over the next several years; 10-20% of the raised $60-64B 2026 capital budget goes to advanced packaging, testing and mask making.

quarterly_data.signal: GLASS SUBSTRATE / NEXT-GEN PACKAGING STATUS: asked about progress on glass core, glass substrate and glass carrier alongside the roadmap to beyond-14x-reticle CoWoS, C.C. Wei said 'today, the MAJORITY IS STILL CoWoS... We are developing that alternative, try to LOWER DOWN THE COST. We also work with a SUBSTRATE VENDOR so that our customer can have their product be in the market.' On timing: the previously announced PILOT LINE is being built and 'it will take about ANOTHER ONE YEAR TO BE MATURE so we can put it into the production with our customer' — i.e. glass-based production insertion around mid-2027 at the earliest.

quarterly_data.signal: Fan-out panel-level packaging (FOPLP) for AI: chairman confirms PTI is an AMD AI-chip supply-chain partner providing fan-out PLP solutions and is actively pursuing more AMD AI-chip applications; despite equipment-delivery delays, installation issues and doing new-product qualification in parallel, the program is on schedule and PTI is confident of volume production before the middle of next year, which would make it the world's first company to mass-produce fan-out PLP for AI applications. The former-AUO fab conversion is going smoothly: floor 1 for middle-end/RDL processing, floor 2 for chip-on-panel and mounting packages onto ABF substrates; the G7 panel equipment supporting the AMD program is fully installed and in qualification, with automation being added. PTI showed an engineering sample of a 5x-reticle-size AI package (one reticle = 26x33mm) - it says only TSMC otherwise has this capability - and notes a G7 panel fits about 45 such large AI packages versus 8 to 9 on a wafer, positioning panel output as a complement to foundry wafer-based advanced packaging. FOPLP equipment lead times run about a year plus installation; management estimates a new entrant would need roughly three years from ordering to customer qualification (PTI started fan-out panel work in 2015). In high-end flip-chip BGA, PTI already mass-produces large FC-BGA/MCM and will move a large one-reticle-size chip package into volume production in Q3.

By end market: general semiconductor revenue rose 27% sequentially and over 90% year over year, with all reportable segments up sequentially in general semiconductor; memory demand declined sequentially due to product and customer mix after a 60% increase the prior quarter; automotive and industrial improved 15% sequentially, though industry headwinds are expected to linger through fiscal 2026; aftermarket products and services rose 14% year over year.

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance: for the March quarter K&S expected revenue to increase 15% sequentially to $230 million with gross margin of 49%, non-GAAP operating expenses of $73 million, GAAP EPS of $0.53 and non-GAAP EPS of $0.67. Beyond that, Lester Wong (interim CEO and CFO) said Q3 "definitely will be sequentially better than Q2" and that "the second half of FY '26 should be about 15% to 20% better than the first half", calling that the visibility he has today with possible upside. He expected gross margin for the rest of FY '26 to be around 49% to 50% (the long-standing target is 50%), helped by more demand for higher-margin high-performance ball bonders and by volume absorption.

quarterly_data.signal: Demand and utilisation: management reported improving order activity with additional visibility through fiscal 2026. General semiconductor utilisation is estimated to remain over 80%, and ball bonding utilisation in the memory market exceeds 85%, up from the mid-70% range last year, which management read as a healthy capacity environment for its NAND assembly solutions; it added "While AI-related workloads are driving capacity tightness across the memory market", they are also driving new packaging for cost-effective stacked DRAM and emerging high-bandwidth flash (HBF). By region: China is over 90%, the rest of Asia around 80%, Southeast Asia still in the 70% range but rising, North America over 80% and North America plus Europe about 80%. Lester Wong said "data center is basically the central driver for this cycle": K&S has been taking share in leading-edge logic for data centers, is already in production for some of the most advanced heterogeneous logic applications, its core ball bonders serve data-center infrastructure, networking, communication, power and storage chips, and enterprise SSD use in data centers is also helping the memory business.
quarterly_data.figure: general semiconductor utilisation over 80%; memory ball bonding utilisation exceeds 85% (up from the mid-70% range last year); China over 90%

quarterly_data.signal: HBM: K&S extended its thermo-compression (TCB) footprint into high-bandwidth memory and shipped its first HBM system to a large memory customer during the December quarter; the system went to the customer's facility in the U.S. and is undergoing qualification. The next milestone is hopefully another system shipment; "There may be POs within FY '26, but I think actual production would be more FY '27" and "I think volume production will be in fiscal '27." Management continues to anticipate "Fluxless thermocompression remain a strong alternative to hybrid bonding for the next-generation HBM needs."
quarterly_data.figure: first HBM system shipped in the December quarter, in qualification; volume production expected in fiscal '27

quarterly_data.signal: High-bandwidth flash (HBF): asked whether HBF is a TCB or vertical-wire opportunity, Lester Wong said "it is a TCB play, not for vertical wire" (probably the APTURA tool). HBF is designed to merge NAND-level capacity with HBM-class performance and targets to match HBM bandwidth with 8 to 16x capacity; it is still in early stages, multiple packaging technologies may be used, and K&S is exploring it with a few customers. The next milestone would probably be shipping a system before a PO, and commercial timing is "probably be more of a CY '27 play."
quarterly_data.figure: HBF targets 8 to 16x capacity at HBM bandwidth; expected to be more of a CY '27 play

quarterly_data.signal: Vertical wire (K&S says it pioneered the technology) is its other DRAM opportunity, a cost-effective die-stacking alternative for bandwidth; customer feedback is positive and management anticipates strong sequential growth in both TCB and vertical wire over the coming years. It is gaining traction with some volume possibly in the latter half of FY '26 but expanding much more in FY '27; "We're currently working with 8 customers in Korea, China and the U.S. on this." Together with the HBM system shipped to the leading memory maker, this is K&S's move from its traditionally NAND-heavy memory business into DRAM.
quarterly_data.figure: vertical wire: working with 8 customers in Korea, China and the U.S.; expanding much more in FY '27

quarterly_data.signal: TCB installed base and capacity: "We have 120 TCBs in the field, and half of those are Fluxless." K&S's TCB business started with an IDM in the U.S., moved on to foundry, and is now seeing "quite a lot of demand from OSAT"; advanced TCB capacity is in demand throughout the customer base and the Advanced Solutions segment is expected to grow strongly this year. The formic-acid Fluxless TCB (FTC) is already qualified and in high-volume production, while qualification of the plasma FTC version is under way with a customer. K&S is expanding its Singapore facility "to increase our Fluxless thermocompression production capacity by 3x."
quarterly_data.figure: 120 TCBs in the field, half Fluxless; Singapore expansion to increase Fluxless TCB production capacity by 3x

quarterly_data.quarter: Han's CNC Technology IR activity record: 2026-004 (09-17-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (IR record): for AI-server PCBs, its high-torque spindle mechanical drilling and upgraded 3D back-drilling are widely used at customers, enabling volume processing of 31.5:1 aspect-ratio through-holes and 0-4mil back-drilling (CPK above 1.33); its LDI holds line-width variation within 3μm for impedance control within ±7%, and its four-wire testers are gaining share. For 800G/1.6T optical-module substrate-like boards, its cold-laser drilling stably processes 50μm dense micro-vias, its CCD six-axis router reaches ±25μm and its micro-needle tester handles 1.6T module BGA pitch of 150μm or less; these products have passed validation at leading downstream customers and are delivered in volume.

quarterly_data.signal: Power demand from AI is the stated driver across the group's energy businesses. The filing cites the IEA forecast that electricity demand grew 3.0% in 2025 and will average 3.6% a year from 2026 to 2030 on electrification and large data-center construction, and notes that 2025 gas combined-cycle orders rose 41% year on year to 96GW and that gas combined cycle will keep expanding to cover data-center load. The fuel-cell unit says surging data-center power demand is creating grid bottlenecks and pushing buyers toward behind-the-meter distributed generation, for which modular fuel cells that can be installed quickly and scaled with each data-center phase are presented as the practical solution, with the largest opportunity in exports to United States data centers; cumulative Korean fuel-cell installations reached 1,477MW at 06-30-2026 of which Doosan supplied 731MW, about 50%.

JPY 2.3 billion; contract dated September 30, 2026, property handover March 31, 2027. The company says the Nagaoka Factory will mark 40 years of operation in 2033 and is expected to undergo major upgrades, and the land expands its options for renovating the factory, as part of strengthening its group-wide supply structure for expanding AI-driven demand for electronic substrates and components. MEC states it has a particularly high market share in chemicals for the package-substrate manufacturing process. Impact on results for the fiscal year ending December 2026 is described as immaterial.
quarterly_data.figure: Approx. JPY 2.3 billion (land and buildings); handover March 31, 2027

quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 (January-December 2025) results (annual securities report): net sales JPY 20,947,752 thousand (+14.9%), a record high, of which chemicals JPY 20,211,797 thousand (+15.6%); gross profit JPY 12,977,222 thousand, gross margin 62.0% (+1.1 points); operating income JPY 5,748,013 thousand (+26.0%), operating margin 27.4% versus 25.0% the prior year; ordinary income JPY 6,051,506 thousand (+29.2%); profit attributable to owners of the parent JPY 5,028,609 thousand (+119.4%). Management attributes the sales growth to steady demand for chemicals for advanced semiconductor package substrates, mainly generative-AI related, and for general-purpose package substrates for PCs and smartphones, and the profit growth to higher chemical shipment volumes and steady demand for high-margin products. Overseas sales ratio 65.1% (61.7% the prior year); including sales to overseas customers through domestic Japanese agents, 80.3% (77.3%).
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025 net sales JPY 20,947,752 thousand (+14.9%); operating income JPY 5,748,013 thousand (+26.0%); operating margin 27.4%

quarterly_data.signal: Products (annual securities report, FY2025): MEC's chemicals are mainly metal surface-treatment agents and account for more than 90% of both sales and operating income. The company states its chemicals hold a high share in manufacturing semiconductor package substrates for computers and COF substrates for displays; its CZ series adhesion promoter roughens the copper surface so copper and resin do not delaminate under chip heat, and is adopted by semiconductor package substrate makers worldwide; it is also developing a chemical-adhesion technology that improves copper-resin adhesion without roughening. In FY2025 the CZ series (ultra-roughening adhesion promoter with a high share in package substrates) performed strongly on generative-AI, PC and smartphone demand; the V-Bond series (multilayer boards) and EXE series (displays) were roughly flat; the SF series (displays) declined. Management expects growth in the number of semiconductor package substrates on strong semiconductor demand, and larger, higher-layer-count substrates for higher performance, to drive demand for the CZ series and for products for leading-edge technology.
quarterly_data.figure: Chemicals more than 90% of sales and operating income

quarterly_data.signal: Segments, FY2025 (annual securities report; sales to external customers): Japan JPY 7,827,186 thousand (+8.6%), segment profit JPY 4,301,885 thousand (+23.7%) - demand for products for advanced package substrates, mainly generative-AI related, kept expanding, and sales to Korea through Japanese agents were firm on the recovery in memory package substrates; Taiwan JPY 3,887,138 thousand (+16.9%), led by advanced (generative-AI) and general-purpose (PC, smartphone) package substrates; Zhuhai (China) JPY 2,780,493 thousand (+20.6%) on generative-AI, smartphone and PC demand; Suzhou (China) JPY 3,953,110 thousand (+9.9%) on smartphone, PC and display demand; Europe JPY 1,393,086 thousand (+40.8%) - demand varied by customer, but the region moved out of inventory adjustment, plus temporary demand for materials it handles; Thailand JPY 1,106,736 thousand (+36.5%) - automotive was weak but satellite-communication products and package-substrate demand were firm as board makers step up capex in Southeast Asia. Production (manufacturing cost of electronic-substrate chemicals) totalled JPY 11,069,849 thousand (+16.1%). Orders received are not disclosed because the company mainly produces to forecast, and no customer accounted for 10% or more of net sales.
quarterly_data.figure: Japan JPY 7,827,186 thousand (+8.6%); Taiwan JPY 3,887,138 thousand (+16.9%); production JPY 11,069,849 thousand (+16.1%)

quarterly_data.quarter: Qnity Electronics press release: Qnity Expands AI-Driven Advanced Packaging Capabilities (08-25-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Qnity introduced an integrated advanced-packaging materials platform combining metallization, bumping, dielectric and fine-line patterning for 2.5D, 3D and panel-level architectures, aimed at CoWoS, EMIB and HBM, which 'require precise plating height control and superior coplanarity'. It supports tin-silver (SnAg) micro-bumps, copper-to-copper direct and hybrid bonding and high-resolution dielectric and patterning processes, 'enabling 2 µm line/space metallization'. Named products: Intervia CB1000+ / CB3000 copper; Solderon TS8000 series SnAg micro-bump plating for HBM; Riston WBR5000 thick dry film photoresist for 2.5D packaging (200–320 μm film thickness, high-aspect-ratio copper pillar plating); Cyclotene dry film photo-imageable dielectric for fan-out panel-level packaging and advanced substrate, which fills through-glass vias (TGVs) for glass core substrates. Chuck Xu, President, Interconnect Solutions: AI, chiplets, HBM, 3D stacking and heterogeneous integration are creating demand for integrated solutions spanning advanced packaging and thermal management. No customers, volumes or availability dates are named.
quarterly_data.figure: 2 µm line/space metallization; Riston WBR5000 200–320 μm film thickness

quarterly_data.quarter: Qnity Electronics press release: Qnity Introduces Stackplane CMP Slurry Platform for (08-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Qnity introduced the Stackplane family of CMP slurries for advanced packaging, combining commercialized products with next-generation slurry technologies: SP1000 and SP2000 series for hybrid bonding, SP3000 series for TSV applications, SP4000 series for polymer CMP and SP5000 series for emerging technologies such as panel-level through-glass vias (TGVs) and glass CMP. Qnity notes that many advanced packaging programs require numerous distinct CMP steps, including planarization following hybrid bonding and TSV integration. Kate Dei Cas, President, Semiconductor Technologies: 'Qnity already offers one of the industry's broadest portfolios for advanced packaging' (company claim). The slurries are evaluated in Qnity's polishing lab in Hsinchu, Taiwan. No customers or volumes are named.
quarterly_data.figure: Stackplane SP1000 to SP5000 series (hybrid bonding, TSV, polymer CMP, glass / TGV)
